questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate the difference between India’s share of world exports of rice in 2010 and 2022. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 1 and Figure 2) show that the rice export ban by India in 2022 is likely to have had a significant impact on the world price of rice.

Extract B (line 19) states: ‘In Nigeria, the demand for rice is very price inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain how the Indian export ban is likely to have affected the market for rice in Nigeria.
All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to result in a fall in the market price of rice?
options: Farmers releasing less rice for sale
Good weather conditions for growing rice
More wheat being planted instead of rice
The removal of a subsidy for growing rice

questions.questionText: Figure 4, shows the original demand (D1) and supply (S) in the market for jewellery. D2 shows the demand after an increase in incomes. After the increase in incomes, the market price of jewellery will rise due to
options: excess demand at price P1.
excess supply at price P1.
increased average cost of producing jewellery.
increased competition between sellers.

questions.questionText: Land is an example of a resource that is in composite demand. Land can be used to produce soya beans and for forestry. Between January 2019 and January 2024, the market price of soya beans increased by almost 40%. This was largely driven by the rise in demand for soya beans. Which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C or D, shows the most likely effect of the increase in demand for soya beans on the market for land that is used for forestry?
Figure 4 shows a market for houses to rent. The current average monthly rent in the market is R1. Why is this market in disequilibrium at an average monthly rent of R1?
options: Market forces are likely to encourage landlords to reduce the rent they charge
Market forces are likely to lead to an increase in the average rent and fewer houses available for tenants
Some landlords who would like to rent houses out at R1 cannot find tenants
Some potential tenants who would like to rent a house at R1 cannot find a house to rent

questions.questionText: Inflation resulted in a basket of goods and services that cost £100 in 2015 costing £112 in 2021. Using this information and the data in Extract A (Table 1), calculate the percentage increase in average university rent, in real terms, between 2015 and 2021. Give your answer to one decimal place.

Extract B (lines 3–4) states that ‘Universities have expanded the number of places on offer to students, but the supply of student accommodation is highly inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain the impact of the increase in the number of students attending university on the market for student accommodation.
The market for barley is no longer in equilibrium due to an increase in demand for barley. This is most likely to lead to
options: a fall in the price of barley and a leftward shift of the supply curve.
a fall in the price of barley and a movement along the supply curve to the left.
a rise in the price of barley and a movement along the supply curve to the right.
a rise in the price of barley and a rightward shift of the supply curve.

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the original demand (D) and supply (S) curves for pints of milk. To help farmers, the government introduces a minimum price of 80p for a pint of milk. Which one of the following is most likely to result from the imposition of this minimum price?
options: Profits of farmers from selling milk will increase by £1 million
The revenue received by farmers will increase by 30p per pint
There will be excess demand of 40 million pints
Total revenue from the sales of milk will increase by £100 million

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the demand (D) and supply (S) curves for scooters. Market equilibrium is initially at E, the intersection of D1 and S1. The government announces a cut in the indirect tax on scooters and an increase in the indirect tax on bicycles, a substitute for scooters. Which one of the following is most likely to be the new equilibrium in the market for scooters?
options: F
G
H
I

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the demand for lemons. The fall in price and increase in the quantity demanded of lemons could have been caused by
options: a fall in the price of a substitute for lemons, oranges.
a rise in the price of lemonade.
a reduction in the price of a complement for lemons, fish.
favourable weather leading to a record harvest.

questions.questionText: Explain possible reasons for fluctuations in the world market price of tea.

Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate, in percentage terms, how much more expensive a basket of groceries at Waitrose was than at Lidl in April 2020. Give your answer as a percentage to two decimal places.

Weekly sales of doughnuts are 20 000 and the market price is £1.20 per doughnut. The government introduces a new indirect tax of 15p per doughnut. Sales fall to 16 000 a week and the price rises to £1.30 per doughnut. The share of the total weekly tax that is borne by doughnut producers is

Figure 2 shows supply and demand in the market for beef. D1 shows the initial demand and S1 the initial supply curve. Which one of the following combinations of events would be most likely to cause demand to shift from D1 to D2 and supply from S1 to S2?
options: A fall in the price of chicken and an increase in the price of animal feed
A fall in workers’ wages and a shift in preferences towards vegetarian food
Higher disposable incomes and a fall in farm productivity
Higher rents for farmland and health warnings about eating red meat

questions.questionText: A shift left in the supply curve causes a market to be in disequilibrium at the original market price because
options: consumers cannot buy as much as they would like.
consumers no longer wish to buy the same quantity.
firms are willing to supply more of the good.
firms experience an increase in their stocks of the good.

questions.questionText: Figure 6 represents the market for sugar in a country. It shows the demand (D) curve and two supply (S1 and S2) curves in the market for sugar before and after the imposition of an indirect tax on sugar. According to Figure 6, which one of the following combinations: A, B, C, or D, is correct?

Figure 8 shows two demand (D1 and D2) curves and two supply (S1 and S2) curves in the market for tea. Tea and coffee are substitutes. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely explanation of the move from E1 to E2 in the market for tea?
options: A fall in the price of tea and a rise in productivity in coffee production
A rise in the price of coffee and an increase in the cost of producing tea
An increase in competition in the market for tea and a fall in the price of coffee
The removal of a subsidy to tea producers and a fall in the price of coffee

questions.questionText: Table 3 shows the demand for and supply of oranges at a range of prices between 10 pence and 30 pence. As a result of an increase in consumers’ incomes, the demand for oranges increases by 25% at each of the prices shown in Table 3. After the rise in incomes:
options: at a price of 10 pence, excess demand increases by 50%.
at a price of 30 pence, excess supply falls by 75%.
the equilibrium market price increases by two-thirds.
the price elasticity of demand increases by 25% at each price.

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows demand (D) and supply (S) in the market for electric cars. Demand is initially at D1 and supply at S1. Other things remaining the same, which one of the following combination of events could have caused demand to shift from D1 to D2 and supply from S1 to S2?
options: Greater availability of roadside chargers for electric cars and a rise in workers’ wages
Higher petrol prices and an increase in workers’ productivity
Introduction of a road pricing scheme for all vehicles and higher diesel fuel prices
Lower rail and bus fares and the use of new technology for electric car production

questions.questionText: In the market for apples, at the current market price of £3 per kilo, consumers buy 5000 kilos and farmers produce 6000 kilos each week. It can be concluded that
options: consumers are unaware of the positive externalities from eating apples.
the government must have set a maximum price for apples.
the prices of substitute fruit such as oranges and pears have risen.
there is disequilibrium in the apple market and the price is likely to fall.

questions.questionText: A government decides to set a minimum price for plastic bottles of water above the current market price. The most likely impact of the scheme will be
options: a rise in consumption of plastic bottles of water.
a shortage of plastic bottles of water if the price elasticity of supply is zero.
excess stocks of plastic bottles of water.
no excess supply of plastic bottles of water if the price elasticity of demand is zero.

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate the percentage change in the price of construction sand between January 2014 and January 2018. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figures 1 and 2) show that expansion in the global sand market is leading to prices of construction sand rising in real terms.

Extract B (line 18) states that the global trade in sand has been ‘made possible by cheaper transportation’. With the help of a diagram, explain how cheaper transportation and a construction boom in East Asia have led to growth in the market for sand.

The market for crab sandwiches experiences an increase in the price and an increase in the output of crab sandwiches. Which of the following combinations of events is the only one that could have caused these changes?
options: A fall in the price of tuna sandwiches and a fall in the price of crab
A new tax on food packaging and a fall in labour productivity
A rise in the price of prawn sandwiches and a rise in the price of bread
New entry of firms into the sandwich market and a reduction in the minimum wage

questions.questionText: The following supply and demand diagram shows the impact of a government tax on chocolate bars. The amount of tax revenue raised each week is
options: £0.45 million
£0.60 million
£0.75 million
£1.00 million

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows demand and supply in the market for roses. The demand for roses shifts from D1 to D2. Other things remaining the same, it can be concluded that
options: monopoly suppliers have pushed up the price of roses.
the higher price of roses will cause demand to fall back to D1.
the income elasticity of demand for roses is positive.
there is greater incentive to supply roses.

questions.questionText: A government sets a maximum price below the current market price for rented housing. The likely long-run consequence is that
options: fewer people can live in rented housing.
the rationing function of prices will improve.
there will be a fall in supply of owner-occupied housing.
there will be excess supply of rented housing.

questions.questionText: Beef and leather are in joint supply. Changes in farming methods have resulted in a significant fall in the price of chicken, a substitute for beef. All other things being equal, which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C, or D, best illustrates the effects of the fall in the price of chicken on the market for leather?
To what extent, if at all, do the data suggest that houses in the UK were more affordable in 2017 than they were in 2007? You must use the data in Extract C to support your assessment.
Explain the likely causes of the main changes in house prices that have taken place between 2007 and 2017.

The diagram below shows the demand curve (D) and the supply curve (S) in the market for tomatoes. Which one of the following would result in a higher quantity consumed and a lower price charged for tomatoes?
options: A fall in the price of the fertiliser used to grow tomatoes
A hot summer causes consumers to eat more tomato salad
The minimum wage for farm workers is increased
The price of cucumbers falls

questions.questionText: Which one of the following would generate a short-run disequilibrium with excess supply in the market for Cornish pasties?
options: A minimum price for Cornish pasties is set above the current market price
Higher meat prices increase the cost of producing Cornish pasties
More advertising increases the demand for Cornish pasties
The government levies a new indirect tax on Cornish pasties

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the demand curve (D) and two supply curves (S1 and S2) in the market for renewable energy. The renewable energy market is initially in equilibrium at a price of OH. The government then introduces a subsidy for renewable energy. After the introduction of the subsidy, the total amount of money received by the producers from both consumers and the government is
options: OGME2
OHLE2
OHNME2
OJKE2

questions.questionText: At the initial market equilibrium, the income elasticity of demand for fresh chickens is +1.5, and the price elasticity of supply is +1.0. Then there is a 5% increase in consumers’ income. Which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is most likely to show the changes in the market equilibrium price and quantity?

The following diagram shows the impact of a government subsidy for recycling waste which shifts the supply curve from S1 to S2. Which one of the following areas measures the cost of the government subsidy?
options: A B C P1
A B D P2
F C D E
P1 C D P2

questions.questionText: The table below shows the quantities of sandwiches that would be demanded and supplied at different prices. Following a rise in production costs, supply falls by 80 sandwiches at all prices. The new equilibrium price would be
The equilibrium market price of a good increases. The establishment of the new equilibrium at a higher price would most likely result from
options: a fall in the price of a substitute.
a rise in the price of a complementary good.
excess demand at the original price.
new firms entering the market.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the demand and supply curves for new houses. The initial demand and supply are D1 and S1. Other things being equal, which one of the following combination of events is most likely to cause demand and supply to shift to D2 and S2?
options: A fall in mortgage interest rates and a relaxation of planning restrictions
A fall in the price of new homes and a fall in the productivity of construction workers
A fall in the price of rented accommodation and a fall in the price of raw materials
A rise in incomes and a rise in wages of construction workers

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the demand curves (D1 and D2) and the supply curve (S) in the market for good X. The initial market equilibrium is at E1. The increase in market demand from D1 to D2 results in a new market equilibrium at E2. The market mechanism that leads to the establishment of the new equilibrium is based on
options: excess demand for good X at the initial price of P1.
excess demand for good X at the new price P2.
excess supply of good X at the initial price of P1.
excess supply for good X at the new price P2.

questions.questionText: Many agricultural products are subject to large fluctuations in price. One reason why these large fluctuations occur is because the
options: demand for agricultural products is income inelastic in the long run.
supply of agricultural products is price elastic in the long run.
supply of agricultural products is price inelastic in the short run.
demand for agricultural products is price elastic in the short run.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the market demand curve (D) and two market supply (S1 and S2) curves for a good. The initial equilibrium point is at E1. The introduction by the government of an indirect tax per unit of the good results in a new equilibrium at E2. The amount of the indirect tax per unit is measured by the
options: vertical distance FE2.
increase in price P1P2.
the diagonal distance E1E2.
the horizontal distance GE1.
